title: Psalms Chapter 37 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 37 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 37 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 37.

questions.question: In Psalms 37, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Fret not thyself because of evildoers
Delight thyself also in the LORD
Commit thy way unto the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Fret not thyself because of evildoers
questions.explanation: The first command in Psalms 37 is to 'Fret not thyself because of evildoers' as stated in Psalms 37:1.

questions.question: What shall happen to evildoers according to Psalms 37?
options: They shall be cut down like the grass
They shall delight themselves in peace
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be cut down like the grass
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:2 states that 'For they shall soon be cut down like the grass.'

questions.question: What should one do in the LORD according to Psalms 37?
options: Trust in the LORD and do good
Delight thyself also in the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in the LORD and do good
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:3 instructs to 'Trust in the LORD, and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 37 say the LORD will give to those who delight in Him?
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 37:4, if you delight in the LORD, 'he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.'

questions.question: What should you commit unto the LORD according to Psalms 37?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:5 states 'Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him.'

questions.question: What will the LORD bring forth according to Psalms 37?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:6 says 'And he shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light.'

questions.question: What should one do while waiting for the LORD according to Psalms 37?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:7 instructs to 'fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way.'

questions.question: What should one cease from according to Psalms 37?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:8 states 'Cease from anger, and forsake wrath.'

questions.question: Who will inherit the earth according to Psalms 37?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:11 states 'But the meek shall inherit the earth.'

questions.question: What does the wicked do against the just according to Psalms 37?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:12 states 'The wicked plotteth against the just.'

questions.question: What does the Lord do regarding the wicked according to Psalms 37?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:13 says 'The Lord shall laugh at him: for he seeth that his day is coming.'

questions.question: True or False: The meek shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:11 states that 'the meek...shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.'

questions.question: True or False: The wicked shall be cut off.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:9 states 'For evildoers shall be cut off.'

questions.question: True or False: The righteous will be punished according to Psalms 37.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37 does not state that the righteous will be punished; instead, it focuses on the fate of the wicked.

questions.question: True or False: The wicked have drawn out the sword to help the poor.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:14 states that the wicked have drawn out the sword to 'cast down the poor and needy,' not to help them.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 37 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 37 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 37:15, what will happen to the wicked's sword and bows?
options: Their sword shall enter into their own heart, and their bows shall be broken.
Their sword shall be sharpened against the righteous, and their bows shall shoot arrows swiftly.
Their sword shall be lifted in victory, and their bows shall remain strong.
Their sword shall be taken away by the Lord, and their bows shall be given to the meek.
questions.correctAnswer: Their sword shall enter into their own heart, and their bows shall be broken.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:15 states exactly that the sword of the wicked shall enter their own heart and their bows shall be broken, indicating their plans will backfire.

questions.question: What does Psalms 37:16 promise will happen if someone lives righteously as commanded in Psalms 37:15?
options: A little that a righteous man hath is better than the riches of many wicked.
The wicked will prosper and the righteous will fall.
The righteous will have many enemies but will be victorious.
The Lord will make the wicked rich and the righteous poor.
questions.correctAnswer: A little that a righteous man hath is better than the riches of many wicked.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:16 directly follows 37:15 and contrasts the fate of the wicked with the value of what the righteous possess, promising that even little is better than the riches of the wicked.

questions.question: According to Psalms 37:17, who does the Lord uphold?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:17 explains that the arms of the wicked shall be broken but the LORD upholdeth the righteous, showing God's support for those who live right.

questions.question: According to Psalms 37:18-19, what two things are assured to the upright?
options: The LORD knows their days and they shall not be ashamed in evil times.
They will live without trouble and be rich in this world.
They will have many children and great wealth.
They will never experience hardship or famine.
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD knows their days and they shall not be ashamed in evil times.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:18 notes the LORD knows the days of the upright and their inheritance is forever, and verse 19 assures they shall not be ashamed in evil times nor hungry in famine.

questions.question: What does Psalms 37:20 say will happen to the enemies of the LORD?
options: They shall perish and consume away like smoke.
They shall be victorious over the righteous.
They shall be forgiven and blessed.
questions.correctAnswer: They shall perish and consume away like smoke.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:20 clearly states that the wicked and enemies of the LORD shall perish and consume away into smoke, symbolizing their complete destruction.

questions.question: According to Psalms 37:21, how do the wicked and the righteous differ in handling debts?
options: The wicked borrow and pay not again; the righteous show mercy and give.
The wicked pay their debts promptly; the righteous avoid borrowing.
Both wicked and righteous borrow and repay equally.
The wicked lend generously; the righteous refuse to lend.
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked borrow and pay not again; the righteous show mercy and give.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:21 contrasts the wicked who borrow without repaying with the righteous who show mercy and give, highlighting integrity and generosity.

questions.question: What inheritance is promised to those blessed by God according to Psalms 37:22?
options: They shall inherit wealth and possessions.
They shall inherit the kingdom of heaven immediately.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:22 promises that those blessed by God shall inherit the earth, contrasting with those cursed who shall be cut off.

questions.question: According to Psalms 37:23-24, what does the LORD do for a good man even if he falls?
options: He upholds him with His hand so he shall not be utterly cast down.
He allows him to fall completely to learn humility.
He removes him from his path.
He punishes him for his mistakes.
questions.correctAnswer: He upholds him with His hand so he shall not be utterly cast down.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:24 states that though the good man falls, the LORD upholds him with His hand, preventing complete downfall.

questions.question: What personal testimony does the psalmist give in Psalms 37:25 about the righteous?
options: He has not seen the righteous forsaken nor their seed begging bread.
He has seen the righteous suffer greatly without help.
He has witnessed the righteous losing all their possessions.
He has seen the righteous abandoned by God.
questions.correctAnswer: He has not seen the righteous forsaken nor their seed begging bread.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:25 provides the psalmist's experience that he has never seen the righteous forsaken or their descendants begging for bread, affirming God's provision.

questions.question: According to Psalms 37:26, what character trait is attributed to the righteous?
options: He is ever merciful and lendeth.
He is fearful and hesitant to help others.
questions.correctAnswer: He is ever merciful and lendeth.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:26 describes the righteous as merciful and lending to others, showing generosity and kindness.

questions.question: What two commands are given in Psalms 37:27 for a lasting dwelling?
options: Depart from evil, and do good; and dwell for evermore.
Pray continually and fast regularly; and dwell in peace.
Give alms and attend the temple; and dwell in the land.
Seek riches and build strong houses; and dwell with honor.
questions.correctAnswer: Depart from evil, and do good; and dwell for evermore.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:27 commands to depart from evil and do good, promising that those who do so will dwell forevermore.

questions.question: According to Psalms 37:28, what does the LORD love and how does He treat His saints?
options: The LORD loveth judgment and forsaketh not His saints; they are preserved forever.
The LORD loveth riches and forsaketh the poor; He punishes sinners.
The LORD loveth pride and forsaketh the humble; He tests His saints.
The LORD loveth silence and forsaketh the loud; He hides His saints.
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD loveth judgment and forsaketh not His saints; they are preserved forever.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:28 clearly states the LORD loves judgment and does not forsake His saints, preserving them forever.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 37:23 says the steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD and He delights in his way.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:23 explicitly states that the LORD orders the steps of a good man and delights in his way.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 37:21 teaches that the wicked are generous and always repay their debts.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:21 states the wicked borrow and pay not again, showing a lack of generosity and integrity.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 37:20 promises the wicked will inherit the earth and be satisfied in famine.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:20 states that the wicked shall perish and consume away; it is the righteous who shall not be ashamed or hungry in famine (verse 19).

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 37 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 37.

questions.question: According to Psalms 37:29, who shall inherit the land and dwell therein forever?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:29 explicitly states, 'The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein for ever.'

questions.question: What does the mouth of the righteous speak according to Psalms 37:30?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:30 says, 'The mouth of the righteous speaketh wisdom, and his tongue talketh of judgment.'

questions.question: In Psalms 37:31, what is said to be in the heart of the righteous?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:31 states, 'The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 37:33, what will the LORD not do to the righteous when judged?
options: Leave him in the hand of the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:33 says, 'The LORD will not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him when he is judged,' indicating both protections.

questions.question: What promise is given in Psalms 37:34 to those who wait on the LORD and keep His way?
options: He shall exalt thee to inherit the land
They shall be delivered from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He shall exalt thee to inherit the land
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:34 states, 'Wait on the LORD, and keep his way, and he shall exalt thee to inherit the land.'

questions.question: What is the fate of the wicked as described in Psalms 37:36?
options: He passed away and could not be found
questions.correctAnswer: He passed away and could not be found
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:36 clearly states, 'Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'yashab' (יָשַׁב) in Psalms 37:29 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'yashab' means 'to dwell or sit,' fitting the context in Psalms 37:29 where the righteous shall 'dwell therein for ever.'

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in Psalms 37:35-36 describing the wicked like a green bay tree that passes away?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:35 uses a simile comparing the wicked to a green bay tree, a direct comparison using 'like' or 'as.'

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the righteous inheriting the earth as seen in Psalms 37:11?
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:5 states, 'Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth,' directly echoing Psalms 37:11's theme.

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse connects to the promise in Psalms 37:34 about waiting on the LORD and inheriting the land?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:31 speaks of those who wait on the LORD renewing their strength, connecting to the waiting and inheritance promise in Psalms 37:34.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Psalms 37:29, which states 'The righteous shall inherit the land'?
options: For the LORD loveth judgment, and forsaketh not his saints
Depart from evil, and do good
He is ever merciful, and lendeth
Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down
questions.correctAnswer: For the LORD loveth judgment, and forsaketh not his saints
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:28 immediately precedes 37:29 and says, 'For the LORD loveth judgment, and forsaketh not his saints.'

questions.question: What type of parallelism is present in Psalms 37:38, 'But the transgressors shall be destroyed together: the end of the wicked shall be cut off'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:38 shows synonymous parallelism where two lines express the same idea in different words.

questions.question: How does Psalms 37:39 portray the LORD's role in the life of the righteous during trouble?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:39 states, 'the salvation of the righteous is of the LORD: he is their strength in the time of trouble.'

questions.question: Which literary device is employed in the contrast between the fate of the wicked and the righteous throughout Psalms 37?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37 uses inclusio by framing the psalm with the contrasting fates of the wicked and righteous, creating a literary envelope.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 37:40 states that the LORD will help and deliver the righteous because they trust in Him.
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:40 clearly states, 'he shall deliver them from the wicked, and save them, because they trust in him.'

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 37 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 37 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 37:3 teach about the believer's relationship with God?
options: Trust in the LORD and do good leads to provision and security
Faith alone without works is sufficient for salvation
Good works earn salvation independently of God’s grace
The righteous will always be free from suffering in this life
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in the LORD and do good leads to provision and security
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:3 states, 'Trust in the LORD, and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed.' This teaches the doctrine that trusting God combined with good deeds results in God's provision and security for the believer.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s justice is taught in Psalms 37:13?
options: The Lord will mock the wicked because their judgment is certain
God is indifferent to the fate of the wicked
The wicked will ultimately triumph over the righteous
God’s justice is delayed and uncertain
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord will mock the wicked because their judgment is certain
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:13 says, 'The Lord shall laugh at him: for he seeth that his day is coming,' showing the doctrine that God’s justice is sure and that He will deride the wicked in their punishment.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the inheritance of the earth is presented in Psalms 37:11?
options: The meek shall inherit the earth and enjoy abundant peace
Only the wealthy will inherit the earth
Inheritance of the earth is a reward for political power
The earth is inherited by those who manipulate wicked devices
questions.correctAnswer: The meek shall inherit the earth and enjoy abundant peace
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:11 states, 'But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace,' teaching the doctrine that humility and meekness are rewarded with peace and inheritance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 37:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:18 says, 'The LORD knoweth the days of the upright,' demonstrating God's omniscience—His complete knowledge of the lives of the righteous.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Psalms 37:40?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:40 states, 'And the LORD shall help them, and deliver them... because they trust in him,' highlighting God's faithfulness to deliver and help those who trust in Him.

questions.question: How does Psalms 37:20 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine judgment?
options: It illustrates the final destruction of the wicked consistent with eschatological judgment
It teaches that the wicked will always prosper without consequence
It suggests that divine judgment is arbitrary and unpredictable
It emphasizes human ability to escape divine judgment through works
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the final destruction of the wicked consistent with eschatological judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:20 describes the wicked perishing 'into smoke,' which typifies the biblical theme of final eschatological judgment where the wicked are ultimately destroyed.

questions.question: In what way does Psalms 37:4 prepare for New Testament teaching on delighting in God?
options: It anticipates the NT promise that God grants the desires of those who delight in Him
It contradicts NT teaching by emphasizing self-reliance
It focuses exclusively on Old Testament ceremonial law
It teaches that desires are irrelevant to the believer’s walk
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the NT promise that God grants the desires of those who delight in Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:4 states, 'Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart,' which anticipates NT teaching about the blessedness of delighting in God and receiving His blessings.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 37:9 and Psalms 37:29 teach about the inheritance promised to the righteous?
options: Those who wait on the LORD shall inherit the earth and dwell therein forever
Inheritance is conditional only on human effort without divine involvement
The wicked ultimately inherit the earth instead of the righteous
Inheritance is a metaphor for material wealth only
questions.correctAnswer: Those who wait on the LORD shall inherit the earth and dwell therein forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:9 says 'those that wait upon the LORD... shall inherit the earth,' and Psalms 37:29 states 'The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein for ever,' together teaching the doctrine of the eternal earthly inheritance for the righteous who trust God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 37:23 and Psalms 37:24 teach about God's guidance and sustaining of the righteous?
options: The LORD orders the steps of the righteous and upholds them even when they fall
The righteous fall permanently without divine help
God’s guidance is random and unreliable
The righteous must sustain themselves without God’s intervention
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD orders the steps of the righteous and upholds them even when they fall
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:23 states 'The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD' and 37:24 says 'Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him,' teaching God's providential guidance and sustaining grace.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 37:21 and Psalms 37:26 teach about the character of the righteous in relation to mercy and generosity?
options: The righteous show mercy and lend generously, resulting in blessing for their descendants
The righteous are stingy and refuse to help others
Generosity is only for personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous show mercy and lend generously, resulting in blessing for their descendants
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:21 contrasts the wicked who borrow and do not repay with the righteous who show mercy, and 37:26 says the righteous 'is ever merciful, and lendeth; and his seed is blessed,' teaching the doctrine of righteous generosity and its blessing.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 37:1-2 teaches complacency toward evil since evildoers are only 'cut down like grass.' What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches patient trust in God's timing for judgment, not complacency
It encourages believers to ignore evil completely
It guarantees immediate punishment of all evildoers
It suggests that evil will never be judged
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches patient trust in God's timing for judgment, not complacency
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:1-2 warns against fretting over evildoers because they will soon be cut down like grass, teaching the theological truth of trusting God's sovereign timing for justice rather than anxious complacency.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 37:31 teach about the internalization of God's law in the believer?
options: The law of God is written in the heart, ensuring stability in the righteous' path
The law is irrelevant to the righteous
External adherence to law is sufficient without internal change
The righteous often fail because they do not know God's law
questions.correctAnswer: The law of God is written in the heart, ensuring stability in the righteous' path
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:31 states 'The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide,' teaching the doctrine of internalized obedience resulting in a secure walk with God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly reflected in Psalms 37:28 where God preserves His saints forever?
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:28 says, 'For the LORD loveth judgment, and forsaketh not his saints; they are preserved for ever,' demonstrating God's covenant faithfulness in preserving His people eternally.

questions.question: How does Psalms 37:37-38 contribute to the biblical narrative arc of the final destinies of the righteous and wicked?
options: It contrasts the peaceful end of the upright with the destruction of transgressors
It claims both the righteous and wicked share the same fate
It denies any future judgment after death
It suggests the wicked will ultimately be victorious
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts the peaceful end of the upright with the destruction of transgressors
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:37-38 commands to 'Mark the perfect man... for the end of that man is peace,' but 'the transgressors shall be destroyed,' thus reinforcing the biblical theme of divergent final destinies.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 37:5 and Psalms 37:6 teach about divine action in the believer’s life?
options: Committing one’s way to the LORD leads to God bringing forth righteousness and justice visibly
Human plans succeed without divine involvement
God’s action is hidden and ineffective for the believer
Believers are left to accomplish righteousness by their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: Committing one’s way to the LORD leads to God bringing forth righteousness and justice visibly
questions.explanation: Psalms 37:5 says 'Commit thy way unto the LORD... and he shall bring it to pass,' and 37:6 adds 'he shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light,' teaching that God actively manifests righteousness and justice when believers trust Him.
